---
title: "Exercise 4.6"
---


## Solution
1. By Exercise 2.9(1), we can denote that
$$ B = \limsup_n A_n = \bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty} \bigcup_{n=i}^{\infty} A_n.$$
Since the collection of Lebesgue measurable sets is closed under countable uninons and intersection, $B$ is Lebesgue measurable.

2. Let
$$ B_i = \bigcup_{n=i}^{\infty} A_n.$$
Then $B_i \downarrow B$ and each $B_i$ is Lebesgue measurable.
Since $m(B_1) \leq m([0,1])=1$ and $B$ is Lebesgue measurable,
$$\lim_{i \to \infty} m(B_i) = m(\lim_{i \to \infty} B_i) = m(B).$$
Since
$$m(B_i) = m\left(\bigcup_{n=i}^{\infty} A_n \right) \geq m(A_i) > \delta$$
for each $i$, we have
$$m(B) = \lim_{i \to \infty} m(B_i) \geq \delta.$$

3. Since $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} m(A_n) < \infty$, we have
$$ \lim_{i \to \infty} \sum_{n=i}^{\infty} m(A_n) = 0.$$
For each $n$, we have
$$m(B) \leq m(B_n) = m\left(\bigcup_{n=i}^{\infty}A_n\right) \leq \sum_{n=i}^{\infty} m(A_n).$$
Taking the limit as $i \to \infty$, we obtain
$$m(B)=0.$$

4. Let
$$A_n = \left[0, \frac{1}{n} \right].$$
Then,
$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}m(A_n) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n} = \infty.$$
However, since 
$$B = \bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty} \bigcup_{n=i}^{\infty} \left[0, \frac{1}{n} \right] = \bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty} \left[0, \frac{1}{i} \right] = \{0\},$$
we have
$$m(B) = 0.$$
